sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why miracles above nature are drawn down specifically through the revelation of the name Havayah, even though they are the primary vehicle for Divine revelation.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
for seemingly,
that which creations need a miracle is
(not only in order to save them in their time of distress and the like, but also)
in order that there be a revelation of G‑dliness in the world,
and since in miracles that are clothed in nature there is room for error that they are nature,
and the main matter of the revelation of G‑dliness is in miracles that are above nature,
behold, by His lack are included
(seemingly)
also the miracles that are above nature,
and nevertheless,
the drawing down of miracles that are above nature is specifically through the revelation of the name Havayah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the three names—Sha-dai (meaning "I said to My world enough"), Sha-dai (meaning "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature"), and Havayah—correspond to the vessels, the light that relates to vessels, and the light above relation to vessels.

translations.translation: ה)
And this will be understood by prefacing,
that the three matters mentioned above—the name Sha-dai, on the name that I said to My world enough,
the name Sha-dai, on the name that My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature,
and the name Havayah—are in vessels,
in the light that relates to vessels,
and in the light that is above relation to vessels.
And the explanation is,
that this that the coming into being of the world is with measure and limit
(that I said to My world enough)
is because the coming into being is through the vessels.
For the coming into being itself
(the creation of yesh from ayin)
is from the light
[for although the coming into being is through the power of the Awtsmoos,
which alone has the power and ability to create yesh from ayin,
nevertheless,
since the light is like the luminary,
therefore also the light has within it the power of coming into being22],
except that the coming into being as it is from the aspect of the light is in a manner of without limit,
and in order that the coming into being be with measure and limit, it is through the clothing of the light in the vessels23.
And this is that the name Sha-dai, "I said to My world enough," is in the vessels,
for the matter of limitation in the world is through the vessels that limit
(the spreading forth)
of the light.
And the matter of the name Sha-dai, on the name that My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature, is in the light,
that the spreading forth and revelation of G‑dliness,
the matter of the light,
is enough and sufficient for every creature.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the phrase "sufficient for every creature" emphasizes that the light reaches even the lowest creations, demonstrating its infinite and unlimited nature.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the intention of "every creature" is,
both for the most elevated creations,
that the spreading forth and revelation of G‑dliness is sufficient and fills also the lack of the most elevated creations,
and for the most lowly creations,
including those that have no virtue whatsoever and are merely creatures24,
that the spreading forth and revelation is drawn down also into them.
And it can be said,
that from the language "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature,"
it implies that the main emphasis of "sufficient for every creature" is that it is sufficient even for the most lowly creations that are merely creatures.
And it can be said the explanation of this,
that this that it is sufficient in His G‑dliness also for the most elevated creations,
is not so much a novelty and superiority.
For since even the most elevated creations are limited,
behold also the revelation that is sufficient and enough for the most elevated creations,
is a limited revelation.
And the main novelty and superiority is that it is sufficient in His G‑dliness also for the most lowly creations,
for this that the light
(the spreading forth and revelation of G‑dliness)
is drawn down also into the most lowly creations, below which there is no lower,
indicates that it is infinite and without limit,
because of which it is drawn down downward, downward without end.
